# The Myth of the Dancing Moon

Long ago, when the world was new, the Ocean was perfectly still—a vast mirror reflecting the sky. The Moon, young and curious, would gaze down at her reflection each night, admiring her silver glow upon the water's surface.

One evening, the Moon discovered music drifting up from the Earth—the songs of the first people celebrating around their fires. Enchanted, she began to sway in the sky, moving to the rhythm of their drums and voices.

As the Moon danced, her reflection in the Ocean began to shimmer and shift. The Ocean, captivated by the Moon's graceful movements, tried to dance too. She pushed and pulled herself toward the Moon, reaching upward with liquid arms, creating the first waves.

The Moon was delighted to have a dancing partner. From that night forward, she pulled the Ocean close as she waltzed across the sky, and the Ocean responded with rolling waves and crashing tides.

This is why the Ocean is never still—she is forever dancing with the Moon, following her beloved partner's movements across the heavens. And when the Moon is full and bright, the Ocean dances most vigorously, her waves reaching highest in joyful celebration.

# The Weaver's Children

Long ago, when the sky was empty and black, there lived a weaver named Celestia who created the most beautiful tapestries from silver thread. She had seven children who loved to play with her spools of shimmering thread while she worked.

One day, Celestia created her masterpiece—a magnificent tapestry depicting all the wonders of the earth below. She hung it across the entire sky for all to admire. That night, while she slept, her curious children climbed up to examine their mother's work more closely.

The youngest child tugged at a single thread, and it came loose. Delighted, the children began pulling more threads, laughing as they danced with the glowing silver strands. But their play grew wild, and soon the entire tapestry unraveled. Panicked, they tried to weave it back together, but they didn't have their mother's skill.

When Celestia awoke and saw what happened, she didn't scold them. Instead, she smiled. The scattered threads had created something even more beautiful—each strand caught the light and twinkled independently.

"You've created the stars," she told her children. "Each one will shine forever, reminding us that sometimes our mistakes create unexpected beauty."

And so the stars remain scattered across the night sky to this day.

Myth: Long ago, Celestia the Weaver had a daughter named Luna who desperately wanted to learn her mother's craft. But Luna's hands were clumsy, and every tapestry she attempted fell apart into tangled knots.

One night, frustrated by another failed attempt, Luna threw her ruined work into the darkness beyond the sky. The silver threads scattered and drifted downward toward the sleeping earth.

As the threads fell, they caught the wind and began to glow with their own soft light. Some landed on mountaintops, others in valleys, and still others hung suspended in trees and bushes. The people below awoke to find delicate, glowing strands draped across their world.
